description:
Polka Dot Begonia (Begonia maculata) is an attractive houseplant known for its silver-spotted leaves, but it is toxic to cats. The plant contains soluble calcium oxalates, with the highest concentration hidden underground in the roots and tubers. The leaves and trailing stems also carry these toxins, though in lower amounts.

When a cat bites into the plant, the oxalates act as an immediate chemical irritant. This causes an intense burning sensation in the mouth and throat. Because the pain happens right away, most cats will stop chewing before they swallow a dangerous amount. Systemic effects after eating large amounts of root are uncommon in cats; when they do occur, they involve the kidneys (reported mainly in grazing animals), not the liver.

Common signs of exposure include heavy drooling, redness around the mouth, vomiting, and difficulty swallowing. Symptoms from just chewing a leaf are usually mild. Keep this plant out of reach, and contact a veterinarian if your cat eats the roots or if their mouth discomfort does not improve.
name: Polka Dot Begonia
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: soluble calcium oxalates; tubers and roots most concentrated; leaves carry lower levels
Mechanism: soluble oxalates irritate the gastrointestinal lining and, in large quantities, may contribute to kidney crystal formation
Symptoms: vomiting, drooling, and GI upset from leaf ingestion; more severe GI symptoms if tubers are chewed
Decorative aspects (trailing stems, spotted leaves) may attract cats — keep out of reach
Symptoms are generally mild with leaf exposure; contact your vet if tubers were ingested

symptoms.name: Excessive drooling (hypersalivation), redness around the mouth, oral sores, excessive licking of the lips, and an unpleasant burning sensation
symptoms.notes: This immediate irritation is caused by the calcium oxalates within the plant. Because the very first bite produces such an unpleasant and painful sensation in the mouth and throat, cats are usually deterred from taking more than one bite.

symptoms.name: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia)
symptoms.notes: This is a direct physical response to the intense irritation, pain, and potential swelling in the mouth and throat caused by the plant's toxins.

symptoms.name: Vomiting, disinterest in food and water (anorexia), and difficulty eating
symptoms.notes: The cat will often vomit to rid its stomach of the irritating plant material6. In most cases, these symptoms are relatively mild and naturally clear up within about two days.

treatments.description: Providing the cat with water or milk to help rinse out the mouth and wash away the irritating plant material.
treatments.name: Oral Rinsing and Dilution
treatments.notes: This is an immediate, first-line step to help relieve the intense burning sensation, oral pain, and drooling caused by the oxalates in the plant.

treatments.description: The veterinarian may medically induce vomiting to empty the stomach, followed by administering a dose of activated charcoal with a cathartic to bind unabsorbed toxins in the digestive tract.
treatments.name: Emesis Induction and Activated Charcoal
treatments.notes: Because begonias contain soluble oxalates, this procedure is indicated if the cat has ingested more than just a small taste or nibble (especially the highly toxic roots or tubers) to prevent the toxins from being absorbed into the bloodstream.

treatments.description: Injecting fluids directly into the cat's veins for 24 to 48 hours to rehydrate the body, flush the system, and support organ function.
treatments.name: Intravenous (IV) Fluid Therapy
treatments.notes: This is critical if the cat is refusing water due to throat pain or is suffering from dehydration due to vomiting.

treatments.description: The veterinarian will perform a full physical examination and run blood work to assess and monitor the cat's internal organ health.
treatments.name: Physical Examination and Blood Tests
treatments.notes: While begonia poisoning from leaves is typically mild, if the cat ingested the highly concentrated roots or tubers, blood work helps monitor kidney function, since systemic soluble-oxalate effects are renal (and uncommon in cats)

treatments.description: Feeding the cat a bland, mild diet for several days following the exposure.
treatments.name: Mild Diet Therapy
treatments.notes: This allows any irritation and swelling in the cat's throat and digestive system to heal4. Most mild cases of begonia poisoning clear up within about two days.
